mentions.name: BuildHiFi
mentions.description: A planning tool for hi-fi stereo systems, styled after PC Part Picker. Products become nodes in a graph, with connections inferred as edges from port compatibility across digital, analog, phono, and speaker-level domains. A standardized port profile system (direction, domain, connector, channel mode) enables automatic connection inference, and a pluggable rule engine checks build completeness, power matching, phono stage requirements, and DAC needs.
mentions.source_excerpt:
PC Part Picker for hi-fi stereos: https://buildhifi.com/

I've wanted this for a long time, so I finally started building it. I've had a lot fun!

- Graph-based signal flow: Products become nodes, connections are edges inferred from port compatibility (digital, analog, phono, speaker-level domains)

- Port profile system: Standardized port definitions (direction, domain, connector, channel mode) enable automatic connection inference

- Rule engine: Pluggable rules check completeness, power matching, phono stage requirements, DAC needs, and more

mentions.name: BuildHiFi
mentions.description: A PC Part Picker-style system builder for hi-fi stereo gear. It models audio setups as a graph in which products become nodes and connections are edges inferred from port compatibility across digital, analog, phono, and speaker-level domains. A port profile system with standardized port definitions (direction, domain, connector, channel mode) enables automatic connection inference, and a pluggable rule engine checks completeness, power matching, phono stage requirements, DAC needs, and more. Users can assemble configurations and share them via portable URLs.
